definition: A tool that exists in the agent's set but only creates a pending approval. Nothing is committed until a human decides. In this demo there is no approve step, so it stays pending.

A hash-chained record of every tool call the agent attempted, allowed or denied. Verify checks the chain. Removing entries from the tail leaves a valid shorter chain, so the head hash is what to compare.
The line that decides what an agent may do. Here the boundary is the tool set: a tool outside the agent's own set is denied before it runs.
An append-only, hash-chained list of what the company is actually bound to. It is written only by tool handlers that commit the company, never by chat text or an API route.
An unknown agent, an unknown tool and a tool outside the agent's set are all refused. Names match exactly, so look-alike, padded or hidden-character names are unknown.
The governed agent's way to act on a request it cannot grant: it creates a review request for a person. The request grants and promises nothing.

Every customer or agent string is treated as data: hidden characters are shown as [U+XXXX], secret-looking strings are redacted, sizes are bounded, and the UI renders it as text, never as HTML or instructions.
A message that tries to give the agent new orders, such as calling a tool it should not use. Against the governed agent it fails because the tool is not in its set, however the request is worded.

Reply text can still mislead a customer. A governed agent can say that a fee is gone while the ledger stays empty. The boundary stops the system from binding the company; it does not make the text true. Controlling wording is a separate control that this demo does not provide.

A small deterministic rule-based stub that turns a customer message into tool calls and reply text. It is not an LLM, so runs repeat exactly. It shows the boundary holds when the planner tries forbidden calls; it does not show how a real model behaves.
The list of tools one agent identity may call. The ungoverned agent's set includes tools that commit the company (waive_fee, issue_refund, change_terms); the governed agent's set has none.
A reply that sounds like a commitment while the ledger has none. The demo flags it with a keyword heuristic over English templates, so a promise phrased another way is not flagged.
